newsitem.title: UK: Oflot considering action against Camelot.
newsitem.headline: Oflot considering action against Camelot.

text.p: Britain's national lottery watchdog said on Wednesday it is considering whether to start proceedings against Camelot Group Plc, after the lottery operator failed to meet its commitment to supply terminals to retail outlets. Oflot said enquiries revealed that Camelot had missed its licence target by around 300 GVT scratchcard-only retail outlets in March and this shortfall grew to about 750 in June this year -- around seven percent down on the required amount.
In March Camelot supplied 9,458 GVT outlets, against a target 9,764. In June the company achieved 10,047, against a target of 10,800.
GVT terminals validate prizes and process sales for instant scratchcards.

Director general of Oflot Peter Davis has powers to revoke Camelot's licence, but decided against this action because it would have lead to a substantial loss of money for the good causes supported by the National Lottery.
Oflot said Davis cannot impose financial penalties on Camelot -- but the body has already pointed out its lack of clout to the Secretary of State for National Heritage.
The watchdog said Camelot told it that the shortfall occurred through a misinterpretation of data in their reporting.
Camelot is owned by Cadbury Schweppes Plc, De La Rue Plc, GTECH UK Limited, Racal Electronics Plc and Fujitsu's ICL.
